parsed_output.answer: To find the distance of the image formed by a concave mirror, we use the mirror formula: 1/f = 1/v + 1/u. Here, the object is placed at a distance of 10 cm in front of the mirror, so u = -10 cm (negative because the object is on the same side as the incoming light). The radius of curvature (R) is given as 8 cm, so the focal length (f) is half of the radius of curvature, which is f = R/2 = 8/2 = 4 cm. Since it is a concave mirror, the focal length is negative, so f = -4 cm. Substituting these values into the mirror formula: 1/(-4) = 1/v + 1/(-10). Simplifying, -1/4 = 1/v - 1/10. Solving for 1/v, we get 1/v = -1/4 + 1/10 = -5/20 + 2/20 = -3/20. Therefore, v = -20/3 cm, which is approximately -6.67 cm. The negative sign indicates that the image is formed in front of the mirror, which is the real image.
